interface.title: qPCR Fold-Change Analyzer
interface.field: Molecular biology / miRNA qPCR (relative quantification, circulating miRNA biomarkers)
interface.stage_of_work: Data analysis and reporting after a qPCR run, plus planning the next experiment
interface.what_it_is_for: Turn raw Ct values or a QuantStudio/CFX export into checked fold changes: replicate and plasma sample QC (hemolysis, spike-in recovery), normalisation (reference genes with geNorm, spike-in or global mean), ΔΔCt/efficiency-corrected fold changes with group-vs-control statistics, a publication figure, draft methods and results text, an Excel report and a sample-size estimate.

data.note: I used both built-in examples: the tissue miRNA set (Normal/Cirrhosis/HCC, 18 samples, 7 targets, 378 wells, 1 undetermined) and the plasma QuantStudio export (Healthy/HCC, 16 samples, 17 targets, 561 wells, 17 NTC/standard wells removed, cel-miR-39 spike-in). I also uploaded the test file template.csv through 'Upload my file'. Downloads: qpcr_template.csv, qpcr_figure.png, qpcr_figure.svg, qpcr_results.xlsx (binary, so I did not read its contents).

tree.general: Get trustworthy relative expression changes between groups and a reportable result from raw qPCR measurements

features.specific: Sample quality tab: ΔCq(miR-23a − miR-451a) table and dot plot with borderline/high-risk lines; cel-miR-39 Cq against the median ±1 plot; flagged samples pre-filled into 'Exclude samples from the analysis'
steps: set hemolysis and spike-in thresholds in Advanced settings
open Sample quality and read the risk table
find labelled outliers on the dot plots
review or edit the pre-filled exclusion list

features.name: Standard-curve efficiency calculator with per-assay efficiency table
features.general: Enter a dilution series in an editable grid, fit Ct against log quantity to get efficiency, slope and R² with a plot, then enter per-assay efficiencies that switch the quantification model
features.specific: Efficiency calculator tab (Quantity/Ct grid, 'Quantities are already log10' checkbox, Efficiency/Slope/R² metrics and fit plot) → 'Amplification efficiency per assay' editable table → methods text says 'efficiency-corrected model'
steps: edit or paste quantities and Ct values
optionally tick that quantities are log10
read efficiency, slope, R² and the fitted line

features.name: Group-vs-control statistics with selectable test and multiple-testing correction

choose the correction
read fold change, p, adjusted p, significance and omnibus p
serves_tasks: Define the comparison: choose the reference group the other groups are compared with

features.name: Fold-change summary with per-sample ΔCt/ΔΔCt breakdown
features.general: Summarise relative expression per group and target as a geometric-mean fold change with confidence interval and log-scale spread, and expand to the per-sample normalised values behind it
features.specific: Fold changes tab: geometric-mean FC, 95 % CI low/high, mean log2 FC, SEM per target and group; 'Per-sample values (ΔCt, ΔΔCt, fold change)' expander with Target Ct, Reference Ct, ΔCt, ΔΔCt, log2 FC
steps: open the Fold changes tab
read fold change, 95 % CI, log2 FC and SEM per target and group
expand Per-sample values to trace each fold change to its ΔCt and ΔΔCt

features.name: Configurable publication bar chart with export
features.general: Build a grouped bar chart of effect sizes per item, with a choice of scale and error bar, optional data points and significance stars, a title and item order, then export it as raster or vector
features.specific: Figure tab: Y axis (Fold change / log2), Error bars (95 % CI / SEM), Show individual samples, Show significance, Title, Targets in figure (in order), Download PNG (300 dpi) / SVG / PDF

choose the error bar type
toggle points and stars
set the title and target subset/order
download PNG/SVG/PDF

features.name: Auto-generated methods/results text and report export

edit the results draft

download the Excel report
serves_tasks: Get draft methods and results text and a full report

features.name: Sample-size planner from observed variability
features.general: Use the pooled within-group variability of the current data to estimate the replicates per group needed for chosen effect sizes, significance level and power
features.specific: Plan next experiment tab: Significance level (α), Power (80/90 %), Fold changes to detect (1.25/1.5/2/3/4) → table of pooled SD and n per group per target
steps: choose α
choose power
add or remove fold changes to detect
read n per group for each target
serves_tasks: Estimate how many biological replicates are needed to detect a given effect, using the variability in the current data
